newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey widens scope of car import scheme.
newsitem.headline: Turkey widens scope of car import scheme.

text.p: Turkey expanded the scope of an October decree allowing a limited number of duty free car imports by Turkish expatriates to all of its citizens through a new decree published in the Official Gazette on Friday.

The new decree said individuals and institutions living in Turkey would be allowed to bring in one foreign passenger car of up to five years of age from June 1, 1997 if they deposited at least 50,000 marks for one year at state-owned Ziraat Bank by end-1996.
The new decree also allows Turkish residents who open the required accounts to import used machinery of a value equal to the deposited amount.

The first decree published on October 24 led to strong protests by car and parts producers as well as labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector because it had cut demand by creating future expectations of cheaper car imports.
It allowed some three million expatriate Turkish workers in Europe to import a foreign car or machinery under the same terms now extended to all Turks.
Ten percent annual interest will be paid on the special deposit accounts.

The government expects 25,000 duty free car imports in 1997 and an income of 1.3 billion German marks from the expatriates. Such accounts totalling 42 million marks have been opened since late October.

Leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi announced this week it would lay off 1,011 workers from January 2, 1997 on weak demand caused by expectations of cheaper car imports after the first decree.
Tofas will cut its production to single-shift from two on December 2 and put the 1,011 workers on compulsory leave with 76 percent pay until January 2, 1997.
Turkish automotive industry association (OSD) warned of more job losses of between 4,000 and 5,000 in the parts industry following Tofas's decision.
Car output in Turkey has not recovered to 1993 highs since the 1994 economic and financial crises.

Sales of locally produced cars fell 8.5 percent to 139,829 in January-October 1996 when compared to the same 1995 period while imported car sales tripled to 38,789. Domestic car output plunged 32 percent from a year ago to 17,350 in October and ten-month output was down seven percent to 172,964.
